title: Polished stones
summary: Stones grown as solids and broken as real pieces are (shell, petrified wood, pulled candy, a knapped flake) or drawn from an outline (a faceted tumble, an agate nodule), in twenty-four materials printed through them, rendered with a room's light baked once by path tracing: reflections by polish, clear stones' glow and caustics, nacre's sheen, glints that come and go, and the soft shadow each casts; with a walnut tray of sockets lit the same way.
